(1) **Defeat-routine read-once deferral** — `Sonic1SYZBossInstance.defeatDeferralAppliesToThisBoss()=true`: ROM `BSYZ_Defeated` sets `ob2ndRout=6` (Explode) + `GenericTimer=180` then `rts` WITHOUT falling through; `BSYZ_ShipMain` re-reads `ob2ndRout` at the top next frame (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/75, 76 Boss - SYZ Main and Blocks.asm:70-74,154-160`), so the defeat-timer's first decrement lands one frame after the killing hit. The engine selects the defeat routine in the touch-response pass before the boss's own `update()`, so without the deferral the countdown decremented on the hit frame — shifting the whole defeat→ascent→escape sequence (and the escape's `addq.w #2,(v_limitright2)` camera scroll) one frame early (f12490 `camera_x` exp 0x2C00 act 0x2C02). Identical pattern + fix as `Sonic1GHZBossInstance` (note SYZ uses timer 0xB4=180 vs GHZ 0xB3). (2) **Eggman boss persistence** — `AbstractS1EggmanBossInstance.isPersistent()=true`: the S1 Eggman-ship bosses end their routine with `jmp (DisplaySprite).l` (asm:84), never `MarkObjGone`/`out_of_range`, so they are never culled off-screen and self-delete only from their escape routine once `v_limitright2` reaches `boss_*_end`. The escaping ship flies right at 8px/frame (two BossMoves) and outran the camera; the generic `out_of_range` window culled it at ~82 escape frames, freezing `maxX` at 0x2CA4 (f12575) instead of expanding to boss_syz_end 0x2D40. GHZ happened to reach its end boundary just before the cull window, so it was already correct. (3) **No f_lockscreen clear at defeat** — removed `setCurrentBossId(0)` from `Sonic1SYZBossInstance.updateDefeatWait`: ROM `BSYZ_Explode .transition` (asm:440-453) never touches `f_lockscreen`; it stays set through the run to the egg capsule and is cleared only by the Egg Prison (Obj3E `clr.b (f_lockscreen).w`, modelled by `Sonic1EggPrisonObjectInstance` clearing `currentBossId`). Clearing it at defeat dropped the strict right-boundary (`RIGHT_EXTRA` +0x40) early, letting the player overrun v_limitright2+0x128 (f12767 `x_speed` exp 0 act 0x531 — ROM wall-stops at x=0x2E68). All three fixes are object-local to S1 boss classes; no zone/route/frame carve-out, no shared touch/camera code branched on zone. ZERO regression: 9 S1 greens (GHZ1/GHZ2/GHZ3/SYZ2/SBZ3/SLZ2/MZ1/SBZ1/**SYZ3**) + S2 EHZ1 GREEN; all 10 other S1 reds byte-identical (FZ f3907, LZ1 f5745, LZ2 f6418, LZ3 f8499, MZ2 f2823, MZ3 f9917, SBZ2 f2323, SLZ1 f2872, SLZ3 f3249, SYZ1 f4431); `TestRewindCoverageGuard` passes. Command: `mvn "-Dtest=TestS1Syz3CompleteRunTraceReplay" test`. PRIOR: **S1 SYZ3 `f11169 -> f12490` (errors 94 -> 20) — the SYZ boss block-drop "shake" offset now reads the decrementing word timer's low byte (ROM objoff_3C/3D aliasing), so the ship's collision Y oscillates ±2 like ROM and the rolling player's boss-hit bounce fires on the correct frame** (branch `bugfix/ai-syz3-f11169` off develop `ecc2d5472`). f11169 first-error was `x_speed` exp 0x0054 act -00A9 (also `y_speed` exp -0270 act 0x04E0): the rolling player falls onto the SYZ boss ship and ROM applies `React_BossHit` (`neg.w obVelX / neg.w obVelY / asr.w obVelX / asr.w obVelY`, `docs/s1disasm/_incObj/Sonic ReactToItem.asm:259-263`) — `neg(-0xA9)>>1=0x54`, `neg(0x4E0)>>1=-0x270`, exactly ROM. The engine bounced one frame LATE (f11170) because its collision missed the ship by 2px at f11169. Root: during `BSYZ_Lift` (block-drop hold) the ship's display/collision `obY = obBossY ± 2` shake; ROM reads `btst #1,PhaseTimer` where `PhaseTimer` (objoff_3D) is the LOW BYTE of the word timer `GenericTimer` (objoff_3C) — the per-frame `subq.w #1,GenericTimer` overwrites it, so the shake alternates with bit 1 of the decrementing timer (`75, 76 Boss - SYZ Main and Blocks.asm:20-21,264-295`). The engine modeled objoff_3D as a separate static `justReturnedFlag`, so the shake was stuck at +2 (obY 0x0558) instead of alternating; at the React frame (end of f11168, timer=2, bit1 set → -2) ROM's ship sat at obY 0x0554 (top edge 0x053C ≤ player bottom 0x053E = overlap), while the engine sat at 0x0558 (top 0x0540, 2px miss). Fix: `Sonic1SYZBossInstance.updateDropHold`/`updateDropSettle` read `(timer & 2)` / `(timer & 1)` for the shake direction. Object-local to the S1 SYZ boss (S1-only class), no zone/route/frame carve-out, no shared/touch-response code touched. | Last frontier move | **S1 SBZ2 `f2920 -> f6839` (errors 501 -> 21) — SBZ Teleporter (Obj 0x72) now preserves the player's 16-bit sub-pixel fraction through its rise/travel/snap/release phases instead of zeroing it** (branch `bugfix/ai-sbz2-f2920` off develop `fea5311c7`). f2920 first-error was `x` exp 0x118E act 0x118D (1px short); the diagnostic `eng-expected-onObj s62 missing` was a stale `standonobject` byte (status bit3 clear -- the player is airborne under obj_control, not riding). The controlling object is the SBZ teleporter (Obj 0x72, slot 74, subtype 4) which takes `f_playerctrl=$81` and flings the player along a waypoint path. ROM `Tele_Bump` (`move.w d2,obY(a1)`), the `Tele_Bend` waypoint snap (`move.w objoff_36/38,obX/obY(a1)`), the release (`andi.w #$7FF,obY(a1)`), and `loc_167DA` (`move.l obX(a1) += obVelX<<8`, a 16.16 add) ALL write only the x_pos/y_pos PIXEL words and accumulate via the standard 16.16 fixed-point update, leaving the 16-bit x_sub/y_sub intact (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/72 SBZ Teleporter.asm:90-92,110-111,130-141,146`). The engine's `Sonic1TeleporterObjectInstance` instead used `setCentreX/Y` (which zero the sub-pixel) in the rise, snap, and release, and a separate 16.8 accumulator seeded from `playerX << 8` (discarding the sub-pixel) for the travel move. The player runs into the teleporter carrying x_sub=0x8E/y_sub=0x2E; ROM preserves them (capture snaps x_pos to $1194 via `move.w`, sub untouched), so when velX=-0x666 is applied the result is $118E.28; the engine, having zeroed the sub, lands at $118D.00. Fix: rise/snap/release use `NativePositionOps.writeX/YPosPreserveSubpixel`, and the travel step uses the sprite's existing `AbstractSprite.move()` (the exact ROM 16.16 `loc_167DA` add); removed the redundant `posX_16_8`/`posY_16_8` accumulators. Object-local to the S1 SBZ teleporter (S1-only class, SBZ-only object), no zone/route/frame carve-out. ## 2026-06-28 - S2 ARZ2 f549 -> f553 FIXED (Obj28 animal init displays before first ObjectMoveAndFall) - ENGINE FIX (1 file + focused test)

- Branch/worktree: `bugfix/ai-trace-s2-arz2-f549` in `.worktrees/trace-s2-arz2-f549`, based on coordinator commit `429a5deef`.
- Old focused frontier: `TestS2Arz2LevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` first failed at f549 with `obj_extra_s18_x` ROM absent vs engine `0x0679`, 3191 errors. Diagnostic context showed the ChopChop destruction slot set was otherwise aligned: Obj27 Explosion in slot 19, Obj28 Animal in slot 24, and Obj29 Points in slot 25. The mismatch was the animal's first-frame position: ROM kept the animal at the explosion position, while the engine had already applied one `ObjectMoveAndFall` step.
- Root: Sonic 2 `Obj28_InitRandom` initializes Obj28, chooses the animal art/velocity, allocates Obj29 points, and then branches directly to `DisplaySprite`; it does not fall through to `ObjectMoveAndFall` until the next object pass after routine becomes 2 (`docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:24596-24647`). S3K's `Obj_Animal` has the same routine-0 path: `loc_2C924` initializes the animal and jumps to `Draw_Sprite`, with movement starting in `loc_2C9E0` on the next routine-2 pass (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:61049-61129`). S1 is unaffected because it uses the separate `Sonic1AnimalsObjectInstance` implementation. `AnimalObjectInstance` moved on the constructor frame because the engine creates the dynamic object and calls `update()` in that same frame.
- Fix: `AnimalObjectInstance` now tracks `firstDisplayFrame` and returns from its first `update()` without movement, mirroring the ROM init-display pass. No trace data is written into engine state, and the rule is keyed on generic Obj28 routine timing, not ARZ2, a frame number, or a route.
- New frontier: f553, 3183 errors, first error `obj_extra_s18_x` ROM absent vs engine `0x0679`. This is downstream of the aligned f549 animal first-display position and remains in the ChopChop destruction/lifetime window.
- Verification snapshot: `TestS2ObjectOccupancyOracle#arz2ChopChopAnimalDoesNotMoveOnCreationFrame` passes; ARZ2 target moves f549 -> f553; S2 ARZ1/EHZ1/MCZ1/SCZ guard traces pass; CNZ1 remains at its accepted f3906 frontier. The requested cross-game sweeps after integrating the shared-object change are unchanged from baseline: S1 trace classes run 29 tests with only the known four trace failures (MZ2 f2823, MZ3 f16868, SBZ2 f6839, SLZ3 f11325; the `TestS1Mz1SlotLayoutRegression` diagnostic failures remain pre-existing under the broad pattern), and S3K runs 42 tests with 20 pass / 21 failures / 1 error at the prior expected-red first-error signatures.

At f14132 the engine hurt the rolling player (rings 0x19->0, rtn 02->04, rolling 1->0, hurt bounce x_speed 0x0200 / y_speed -0x0400 / `Sonic_Hurt` knockback) on a horizontal MZ Lava Ball (Obj0x14). - DISASM: ROM `ReactToItem` loops objects with `tst.b obRender(a1) / bpl.s React_CheckNext` (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/sub ReactToItem.asm:50-51). obRender bit 7 is set by DisplaySprite DURING the object's own ExecuteObjects pass. Sonic (slot 0) runs ReactToItem before the ball's slot each frame, so: spawn frame 14131 (ball never executed, bit7 clear) -> 14132 React (bit7 still clear, ball's first display happens later this frame) skip -> 14133 React (bit7 set) HIT. Eligibility therefore starts the frame AFTER the child's first own execution.

Generic ROM-state gate (child slot vs parent exec slot), object-agnostic, no zone/route/frame carve-out, comparison-only.

Context showed `gate=offscreenTouch` for s66: `AbstractObjectInstance.isOnScreenForTouch()` used the fixed 32px `.assumeHeight` Y band, but the column's anchor (y~0x3C8) sits ABOVE the camera top (0x3EC) while its 256px body still overlaps the screen, so the band-test marked it off-screen and `ReactToItem` skipped it. ROM `BuildSprites` (docs/s1disasm/_inc/BuildSprites.asm:61-73) computes render_flags bit 7 from the object's own `obHeight` when `obRender` bit 4 (custom height) is set; the geyser column sets `bset #4,obRender` and `obHeight=#256/2=$80` (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/"4C, 4D MZ Lava Geyser and Maker.asm":213-214), so it stays on-screen for the whole 256px column. `ReactToItem` gates on that bit (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/Sonic ReactToItem.asm:50-51). FIX: new `AbstractObjectInstance.usesCustomRenderHeight()` predicate (default false; models the ROM render-flag bit, not a zone id) routes the S1 touch Y gate through `cameraBounds.containsRenderSpriteBounds(preX,preY,halfW,getOnScreenHalfHeight())` when set; `Sonic1LavaGeyserObjectInstance` overrides it (BODY only) and reports `getOnScreenHalfHeight()=$80`. After the fix the gate passes (`scan s66 ... HURT`) — necessary for the hurt to EVER fire. Zero regression (only the geyser body overrides the predicate).

The body Y tracks `head.Y + 0x60`; the lavafall eruption that produces this column is ONE frame late in phase. Measured engine eruption cadence is a rock-steady 254 global frames (= analytical maker cycle: 121 Wait + ChkType + MakeLava + ~112 head-fall + 18 anim3 + Delete); the offset is a CONSTANT phase set at the maker's first execution (ObjPosLoad/camera-order placement timing), not per-cycle drift — exactly the prior bounce's "maker first-execution 1 trace-frame late via shared S1 ObjPosLoad" finding. Fixing it is a broad camera-order/placement-timing change (risks every S1 ObjPosLoad object), out of scope for an object-local geyser fix and not a permissible carve-out.

The engine's `ranGeyserMainThisFrame` defer is therefore NOT a faithful model of Geyser_Main; but removing it alone REGRESSES the frontier f2823->f2819 (1029->1117 err) because it un-masks the CAUSE-2 eruption-cadence offset (the defer cumulatively compensates phase across cycles). ## 2026-06-28 - S1 LZ1 f12463 -> GREEN (end-of-act camera: horizontal level boundary is applied DIRECTIONALLY per ROM MoveScreenHoriz, not as a symmetric clamp) - ENGINE FIX (1 file, shared camera)
- Branch/worktree: `bugfix/ai-lz1-f12463` off `origin/develop` tip `1a5a1e008`. Baseline `TestS1Lz1CompleteRunTraceReplay` first error f12463 `camera_x exp=0x19B3 act=0x19BF` (1 error, span f12463-f12464).

The engine jumped 0x19AD -> 0x19BF in ONE frame (f12463), an 18px move that exceeds the 16px scroll cap — a clamp, not tracking. The signpost (slot 33, Obj0x0D) is already at routine 04 (touched) by f12463, having run `Sign_Touch`'s `move.w (v_limitright2).w,(v_limitleft2).w` to set the left boundary to the right boundary (engine `setMinX(getMaxX())` = 0x19BF). The engine's `Camera.computeNextHorizontalCameraX` returned `clampAxisWithWrap(nextX, minX, maxX)` (plus a redundant second symmetric clamp at the end of `updatePosition`), so the raised minX=0x19BF clamped the tracked 0x19B3 UP to 0x19BF.
- ROM CITE: `docs/s1disasm/_inc/ScrollHoriz & ScrollVertical.asm` `MoveScreenHoriz` applies the boundaries DIRECTIONALLY: `SH_MoveCameraLeft` (camera scrolling left) does `cmp v_limitleft2,d0; bgt SetScreen; move v_limitleft2,d0` (clamp to LEFT bound only); `SH_MoveCameraRight` (scrolling right) does `cmp v_limitright2,d0; blt SetScreen; move v_limitright2,d0` (clamp to RIGHT bound only); the sweet-spot path (`clr.w v_scrshiftx; rts`) applies NO boundary clamp. So while Sonic runs right the camera only ever consults `v_limitright2`; the signpost's raised `v_limitleft2` is invisible and the camera keeps tracking to the right limit (ROM reaches 0x19BF naturally at f12465). `docs/s1disasm/_incObj/0D Signpost.asm` `Sign_Touch`. S2 `s2.asm` / S3K `sonic3k.asm` share the same direction-split structure.
- FIX: `Camera.computeNextHorizontalCameraX` now clamps inside each scroll branch — leftward branch -> `clampLeftBoundary` (minX only), rightward branch -> `clampRightBoundary` (maxX only, with `maxX<minX` SCZ wrapped-domain fallback preserving prior `clampAxisWithWrap` behaviour) — and the sweet-spot path applies no clamp. The redundant symmetric horizontal re-clamp in `updatePosition` (`x = clampAxisWithWrap(x, minX, maxX)`) was removed; the directional branch clamp is authoritative. The `force`/init path still uses the symmetric clamp (ROM LevelSizeLoad clamps both ways at load).

Verified zero regression: S1 complete-run sweep (57 pass, 4 pre-existing reds MZ2 f2823 / MZ3 f9917 / SBZ2 f2323 / SLZ3 f6507 unchanged), S2 EHZ1 GREEN, `TestCamera` (26) / `TestCameraRewindSnapshot` (3) / `TestCameraTargetRebindAcrossRewind` (1) / `TestRewindCoverageGuard` GREEN, S3K critical (`TestS3kAiz1SkipHeadless`, `TestSonic3kLevelLoading`, `TestSonic3kBootstrapResolver`, `TestSonic3kDecodingUtils`) GREEN. - FIX (3 edits, 1 file). `updateAnimation` now mirrors `Anim_Run` exactly: decrement, return while `>=0` (Anim_Wait), else reload duration, then on `afRoutine` (index past the sequence) advance routine leaving the frame, otherwise load `sequence[index]` and post-increment. Constructor replicates the Harp_Main->Harp_Move fall-through (post-init state `animFrameIndex=1, animFrameTimer=3, currentFrame=sequence[0]`). `updateWait` toggle sets `animFrameTimer=0, animFrameIndex=0` (anim-change reset; next update advances to load `frame[0]`) and leaves `currentFrame` at the previous frame until that update, matching the ROM where the bchg/routine change runs in Harp_Wait but Harp_Move advances next frame. ## 2026-06-28 - S1 SLZ1 f3520 -> f4061 FIXED (SLZ2 stays GREEN) - cross-object staircase hand-off honoured ROM SST slot order: a LOWER-slot solid object's new top-landing now observes the rider's pre-re-seat (previous-frame) y. ENGINE FIX (1 file, shared multi-piece path).
- Branch/worktree: `bugfix/ai-slz1-f3520` off `origin/develop` tip `e6452dfb1` (the prior f3250->f3520 child-slot-leak fix). Baseline: `TestS1Slz1CompleteRunTraceReplay` f3520 `y exp 0x04C9 act 0x04CC` (293 err); `TestS1Slz2CompleteRunTraceReplay` GREEN.
- Diagnosis (proof-backed, BizHawk-free; instrumented `processMultiPieceCollision`): the player walks rightward DOWN one descending SLZ staircase (@0x0B10, the engine's HIGHER base slot 0x44) and steps onto an adjacent flat staircase (@0x0B90, the engine's LOWER base slot 0x2D). The engine matches ROM exactly through f3519 and even produces the correct y=0x04C9 on the @0B10 ride at f3520, but then hands the ride off to @0B90 one frame too early (y 0x04C9->0x04CC). ROM `stand_on_obj` ground truth: ROM holds the rider on @0B10's piece (s61, slot 0x3D) through f3520 (x=0x0B83) and only lands @0B90's piece (s40, slot 0x28) at f3521 (x=0x0B84). x matches the engine exactly at f3520 (engine x first diverges only at f4062), so this is NOT an x/sub-pixel drift -- it is a pure object-selection timing divergence at identical x. ROOT: ROM `ExecuteObjects` runs SolidObjects in SST slot order, so @0B90's lower-slot piece (s40) runs BEFORE @0B10's higher-slot ridden piece (s61) re-seats the rider that frame, and therefore tests its `Solid_Landed` against the rider's PRE-re-seat (previous-frame settled) y -- which is 1px too high to land at f3520, deferring the hand-off to f3521. The engine folds each ROM staircase (parent + 3 `FindNextFreeObj` child blocks) into ONE instance and executes from the HIGHEST reserved child slot (needed for the SLZ2 Fan f2554 hand-off); the dynamic pool scattered @0B90's reserved children (exec 0x4B) ABOVE @0B10's (exec 0x49), inverting the ROM slot order so @0B90 ran AFTER @0B10's re-seat and saw the just-applied (descended) y, landing a frame early. (`docs/s1disasm/sonic.asm` ExecuteObjects; `docs/s1disasm/_incObj/sub SolidObject.asm:262-318` Solid_Landed/Solid_ResetFloor; `5B SLZ Staircase.asm:39-96`.)
- Rejected fix (regressed): forcing the folded staircase execution slot to `parent+CHILD_SLOT_COUNT` to restore ROM parent-slot order regressed SLZ2 (Fan f2554 -> y_speed at f2453) AND an earlier SLZ1 staircase (f2338), confirming the highest-reserved-child execution model is load-bearing for the Fan hand-off. Execution-order normalisation is therefore out (folding is lossy for the Fan-vs-staircase-vs-staircase three-way order).
- Fix (1 file, ROM-cited): `ObjectSolidContactController.processMultiPieceCollision` - when a multi-piece object's SST slot is LOWER than the object the grounded player currently rides (a cross-object hand-off where ROM runs this object's SolidObject before the ridden object's per-frame re-seat), gate its NEW top landing on the rider's pre-re-seat y. Detect-only (apply=false) to classify the contact; for a fresh top landing, re-test the landing band at the rider's last recorded post-collision y (`getCentreY(0)` = previous-frame settled position; the live `getCentreY()` already reflects the higher-slot ride's just-applied re-seat) and DEFER the hand-off one frame if the rider had not yet descended into this object's band. Side/corner contacts and same-object piece hand-offs are untouched; the gate is a no-op whenever the engine already executes the lower-slot object first (then `getCentreY(0)` == live y). This models ROM slot order generally rather than carving out the staircase.
- Result: SLZ1 f3520 -> f4061 (293 -> 261 err). f4061 is a SEPARATE, unrelated root: the SLZ Collapsing Floor (Obj0x53, ROM `onObj=0x3F`, `on_object 1->0`) -- engine goes airborne (air exp 0 act 1) where ROM stays grounded on the collapsing-floor fragments. Not staircase-related.
- Cross-game regression sweep (zero regressions): SLZ2 GREEN; SLZ3 f6507 unchanged; non-SLZ S1 reds byte-identical at documented frontiers (LZ1 f5745, LZ2 f8491, LZ3 f8499, MZ2 f2823, MZ3 f9917, SBZ2 f2323); all S1 greens held (GHZ1/2/3, SYZ1/2/3, MZ1, SBZ1, SBZ3, FZ); S2 EHZ1 GREEN; S3K must-keeps GREEN (Aiz1Skip/LevelLoading/Bootstrap/Decoding); `TestRewindCoverageGuard` GREEN; shared multi-piece/solid unit tests GREEN (`CollisionSystemTest` 54, `TestSolidRoutineProfiles` 13, `TestS3kIczSwingingPlatformObject` 8, `TestMGZSwingingPlatformObjectInstance` 4, `TestS1SwingingPlatformSurfaceRegression` 1). The gate fires only for a grounded cross-object hand-off onto a lower-SST-slot multi-piece object, so single-piece platforms and same-object piece hand-offs are unaffected.

## 2026-06-28 - S1 SLZ1 f3250 -> f3520 FIXED (SLZ2 stays GREEN) - SLZ Staircase (Obj0x5B) leaked its reserved child slots on out-of-range unload, exhausting the dynamic SST so the SLZ fireball maker (Obj0x13) reloaded a chunk late. ENGINE FIX (1 file).
- Branch/worktree: `bugfix/ai-slz1-f3250` off `origin/develop` tip `595c3c2fa` (the prior f3053->f3250 staircase trigger-latency fix). Baseline: `TestS1Slz1CompleteRunTraceReplay` f3250 `x_speed exp 0x0200 act 0x0000` (189 err); `TestS1Slz2CompleteRunTraceReplay` GREEN.
- Diagnosis (proof-backed, BizHawk-free): at f3250 the player position is BYTE-IDENTICAL to ROM (`y exp/act 0x03D9`); only the hurt effect is missing. The player should be hurt by a rightward SLZ fireball (Obj0x14) at (0x0BC8,0x03D0). ROM aux ground truth: the responsible fireball spawned at trace-f3162 (X=0x0B18, routine 0) from the (0x0B18,0x03D0) maker (subtype 0x37 = rate 120, ball type 7, velX=$200) and travelled 176px to 0x0BC8 by f3250 (88f old). The engine's equivalent fireball spawned ~55f late (only ~35f old at the same player-position frame, at 0x0B5E), so it never overlapped the player. Root chain: the maker reloads (despawn+respawn via ObjPosLoad) one 0x80 chunk LATE - ROM reloads it when camX first drops to <=0xBFF (chunk 0xB80) per `OPL_MovedLeft` (`objX > (camX&$FF80)-$80`; `docs/s1disasm/_inc/ObjPosLoad.asm` OPL_MovedLeft), the engine only at camL=0xB7D (chunk 0xB00). The engine's backward placement scan (`ObjectPlacementController.spawnBackwardCountered`) HALTS at chunk 0xB80 because a sibling maker's inline create returns FindFreeObj-failure: `allocateSlot()` was exhausted (all 96 dynamic slots allocated) even though only ~45 live objects existed. ROM `slot_dump` at the equivalent f2921 had only 76/96 occupied (20 free). The ~50 phantom-allocated slots were leaked child-slot reservations: `reservedChildSlots` held 39 entries all keyed `id5b(GONE)` (unloaded staircases). `Sonic1StaircaseObjectInstance.reserveChildSlots()` keyed its 3-slot reservation by `getSpawn()`, which returns the per-frame `dynamicSpawn` (the staircase calls `updateDynamicSpawn` every frame), whereas `ObjectManager.freeAllReservedChildSlots` is called on unload with the construction-time placement spawn (`instanceToSpawn`). The identity mismatch meant the reservation was never found/freed; five SLZ1 staircases reloading across the act leaked 3 slots each until the pool was full.

## 2026-06-27 - S1 SYZ1 f4431 -> GREEN (errors 406 -> 0) - Wall-detach slope-resist double-apply: `applyMissedDetachSlopeResist` re-ran walking slope resist using the post-Move inertia on a detach frame where ROM's `Sonic_SlopeResistWalk` was a no-op (frame-start inertia 0). 11th S1 GREEN. ROM `Sonic_MdNormal` runs `Sonic_SlopeResistWalk` first; angle A8 is past the steep exemption (`(A8+$60)&$FF=$08 < $C0`) but `tst.w obInertia / beq.s .return` (01 Sonic.asm:1308-1309) returns because frame-start inertia is 0 -> no resist. `Sonic_Move` then accelerates Right to inertia +$C and `Sonic_AngleSpeed` sets obVelX/Y = (-7,-$A) at angle A8. SpeedToPos moves, `Sonic_AnglePos` rolls the angle A8->C0, `Sonic_SlopeRepel` detaches (|inertia| $C < $280 -> clr inertia, bset InAir, locktime 30) WITHOUT touching velocity, so the ROM-recorded f4431 velocity stays (-7,-$A). The constant +$F/+$16 offset then rode gravity/accel identically for the rest of the slide (f4431 first divergence, position diverges f4433).

S2 `Touch_Enemy_Part2` and the multi-sprite boss path (`s2.asm:85318-85345`) only negate (no `asr`); S3K's `boss_hitcount2`/collision_property paths negate (and also negate ground_vel) without halving. The three boss-bounce sites (player ENEMY at the former inline negate, sidekick ENEMY, and the SPECIAL `applyBossBounce`) are unified through `applyBossBounce`.
- After: GHZ3 f7279 -> f7652 (100 -> 119 errors; the frontier frame is the metric). 0x0418 >> 1 = 0x020C (exact ROM match), 0x01B0 >> 1 = 0x00D8 (exact). The new f7652 root is an unrelated `g_speed` mismatch (expected=0x0297 actual=0x0000) ~373 frames further in.

(1) **Wait-exit camera read.** ROM `BossFinal_Eggman_Wait` reads `(v_screenposx).w` from ExecuteObjects, which runs BEFORE DeformLayers/ScrollHoriz in the level loop (`docs/s1disasm/_inc/DeformLayers (REV01).asm:16-18`), so the boss sees the PREVIOUS frame's camera. The engine's `camera.getX()` during the boss update already reflects this frame's scroll — diag: engine wait-exit at gfc 0x120 (camX 0x2452) vs ROM gfc 0x121 (ROM reads gfc 0x11F's 0x244D at gfc 0x120, exits gfc 0x121). One frame early -> first cylinder select gfc 0x121 vs ROM 0x122. (2) **Cylinder activation-frame extension.** ROM `EggmanCylinder_Action` (routine 2) sets objoff_29, advances obRoutine to 4, but falls through to its body with objoff_3C still cleared to 0 (`clr.l objoff_3C`, `_incObj/85,84,86 Boss…asm:692`) — so the activation frame seats the cylinder at rest (aux: rtn 2->4 at f768 with Y=0x620, first extension f769 at Y=0x61F); the engine extended on the activation frame.

This makes the wait span the ROM-correct number of frames naturally, so the prior `waitFirstFrame` seed-compensation hack (added when only the seed, not the cycle phase, was being corrected) is REMOVED — the seed is now 0x7F at the first select without compensation. (2) `FZCylinder` defers its first extension step one frame after `activate()` (`activationDeferred`): the activation frame runs the routine-2 Action body (extension 0, seated at rest), extension begins next frame.

The new f837 root is the roll-into-boss damage bounce: ROM `x_speed=0x300` (the `move.w #$300` hit-bounce at loc_19F6A) vs engine -0x00F8 (engine bounces one frame late at f838; cylinders ~5px more extended) — a deeper per-frame hit-geometry / cylinder-extension-cadence residual, NOT the wait/activation phase.

## 2026-06-24 - Monitor (Obj 0x26) top-overlap releases a rising rider who JUMPED off it; SLZ3 f1187 -> f1416 (1055 -> 1394)
- Branch/worktree: agent worktree off `origin/develop` 414003281. One engine file: `ObjectSolidContactController.java` (`resolveMonitorContact` rising-rider gate).
- Command: `mvn -o test "-Dtest=com.openggf.tests.trace.s1.TestS1Slz3CompleteRunTraceReplay" "-Dtrace.context.diagnosticChars=full" "-Dsurefire.argLine=-Xmx6g -Xshare:off"`. Baseline f1187 `camera_y` (downstream symptom of player y/air).
- **Root (pinned by stack-tracing every air-clear):** the air-clear bypasses `setAir()` via the direct field write in `setAirAfterObjectHurtLanding()`/`setAir(false)`, reached from `ObjectSolidContactController.resolveMonitorContact:2746` -> `applyObjectLandingState`. At SLZ3 f1187 Sonic does a ROLLING JUMP off a Monitor (Obj 0x26): `doJump()` fires (headroom OK, `air=true`, `rollingJump=true`, `y_speed=-0x680`), but the Monitor's solid pass that frame RE-SEATS him (`resolveMonitorContact` `canLand` branch lands him unconditionally) -> air cleared -> f1188 grounded. ROM `Mon_Solid` -> `SolidObject` gates the top re-seat (`Solid_ResetFloor`/`RideObject_SetRide`) on `tst.w y_vel / bmi` (the `SolidObjectFull` upward-velocity branch `loc_1E198 moveq #0,d4 / rts`, sonic3k.asm:41625-41626), so a rising player crossing the top is NOT re-seated.
- **Fix:** in `resolveMonitorContact`, when `!sticky && y_speed<0 && isJumping()`, return no contact (no lift, no OnObj, no air-clear) — the jump's airborne state + position survive.
- **Why `isJumping()` and not raw y_vel<0 (the MZ1 regression + narrowing):** the pure y_vel<0 gate (ROM's literal `tst.w y_vel`) advanced SLZ3 but REGRESSED MZ1 f2101 -> f1260. At MZ1 f1260 Sonic FALLS (y_speed +0x1C0) and ROM LANDS him on an adjacent intact Monitor (air 1->0, onObj 0->1), but the engine's player has a transient y_speed=-0x1F8 at the monitor pass — a broken monitor's break-bounce flips his y_vel up just BEFORE the landing-monitor's solid runs (an object-execution-order issue: ROM's y_vel is still >=0 at that pass). Instrumented both: SLZ3 f1187 `jumping=true rollJump=true`; MZ1 f1260 `jumping=false rollJump=false`. Adding `&& isJumping()` (ROM `Status_Jump`) scopes the release to the genuine jump-off case and restores MZ1 to f2101/169. ROM's gate is y_vel-only; this is a strict-subset narrowing that does NOT mask the separate MZ1 break-bounce-ordering bug.
- After: SLZ3 f1187 -> f1416 (the new f1416 root is an unrelated Seesaw (Obj 0x5E) ride: ROM `y_speed=0x09E8 air=1 rolling=1` vs engine grounded — onSlot=0x5E).

## 2026-06-24 - Edge-balancing suppresses look-up/down camera pan, computed current-frame (shared player-movement); SLZ3 f1167 -> f1187 (1056 -> 1055)
- Branch/worktree: agent worktree off `origin/develop` 2fc658d51. One engine file: `PlayableSpriteMovement.java` (look gate + new side-effect-free `computeCurrentFrameBalancing()` predicate).

  - NOT oscillation phase: computed the S1 OscillateNumDo sequence in Python — the engine platform position (osc8/osc9 = v8=0x2F56, v9=0x04E2) exactly matches ROM tick 0x0CFA, and ROM `gfc=0x0CFB` is the POST-tick counter (ROM runs `OscillateNumDo` AFTER `ExecuteObjects`, `sonic.asm:2988/3009`, so objects read the prev-frame osc — same as the engine). Platform Y is stable 0x0134 in both. So the platform is correctly positioned.
  - NOT pre-update platform position: tried `usesPreUpdatePositionForSolidContact=true` (ROM Circ_Platform runs PlatformObject before Circ_Types) — INERT, because the platform's Y barely moves frame-to-frame.
  - ROOT (found by logging the `ObjectSolidContactController` top-solid catch): the Y window was satisfied every frame f3331-3334 but the catch was rejected by `isWithinTopLandingWidth`. The CirclingPlatform's collision halfWidth is $18; the generic `Solid_Landed` narrowing subtracts $B -> $0D, so the new-landing X window was [relX d1 in [0, $1A)] which rejected the player at relX=8 (f3332) and only passed at relX=12 (f3335). The width fix alone moved f3332->f3331 (1 frame early); adding HALF_HEIGHT=9 + snap=-1 + zero-reject landed it on ROM's exact frame -> f3353.
- After: SLZ2 f3332 -> f3353. The new f3353 root is a 1px `y` (exp 0x0120 act 0x011F) while the player RIDES the same circling platform (onObj=35) — a distinct sub-pixel continued-ride-seat (obY-9 MvSonicOnPtfm2) residual, not the landing.

Every non-SLZ S1 complete-run byte-identical: GHZ3 f6464/271, LZ1 f5745/662, LZ3 f8499/1525, MZ1 f2101/169, MZ2 f2823/1043, MZ3 f2079/1123, SBZ1 f6081/330, SBZ2 f1447/977, SYZ1 f4430/554, SYZ3 f6065/483, FZ f766/135. ## 2026-06-24 - S1 SBZ spinning platform (Obj 0x69) releases the SolidObject latch on detach; SBZ1 f5532 -> f6081 (frame +549; new root is BallHog, not the platforms)
- Branch/worktree: `bugfix/ai-s1-sbz1-f5532b` off `origin/develop` 1bf821932. One engine file: `Sonic1SpinPlatformObjectInstance.java` (detach path). Committed. Frontier advances 549 frames; the whole spin-platform-row section (f5531-f6080) now matches ROM.

Decode-first ruled out terrain (raw `Blk256_SBZ`=0x0000 at the ground-sensor cells, engine ChunkDesc byte-identical). The cause is the SolidObject **latch**: riding a spinner sets `latchedSolidObjectId=0x69` + `latchedSolidObjectInstance` (instrumented: the @0x1C10 detach at lvlFC 5457 logged `latch=0x69`). `finalizeInlinePlayer` returns early when `latchedSolidObjectId != 0` (a guard for CNZ latch-and-own controllers, ObjectSolidContactController.java:962-964), so on detach it never cleared `Status_OnObj` and never ran the stale-support air transition — the rider stayed pinned to the now-non-solid platform and a same-frame ground check held him grounded.
- **Fix:** in `detachRidingPlayer`, after `clearRidingObject`, drop the latch for THIS instance only (`getLatchedSolidObjectInstance() == this` → `setLatchedSolidObjectId(0)`), and REMOVE the `forceAirOnStaleObjectSupportLoss` call. ROM `.notsolid2`/`.notsolid` (…asm:124-130 spinner, 83-89 trapdoor) does `bclr #3,obStatus(a1)` + `clr.b obSolid(a0)` — clears on-object/standing but does NOT set Status_InAir. The rider goes airborne only on the NEXT frame, when his own grounded floor check (Obj01 precedes the platform in ExecuteObjects, so the engine's inline player-first path matches) finds no floor. Forcing air the same frame went airborne one frame EARLY (tested: f5531/141, air exp=0 act=1). Releasing the latch + letting the grounded check set air is the ROM-faithful timing.
- **After:** SBZ1 f5532 -> f6081. New first error f6081 `x_speed` exp=0x0000 act=-0200: the engine player is HURT (rings 0 vs ROM 11, recoiling) from a BallHog (Obj 0x1E) Cannonball (Obj 0x20) hit that ROM does not take — a distinct, unrelated hit-detection root well past the spin platforms. Error count 150 -> 330 is entirely the newly-reached BallHog cascade; the spin-platform-row frames are now clean.
- **Full sweep (per-class, separate JVMs, frame+count vs develop baselines):** latch release is gated to this instance and Obj 0x69 is SBZ-only, so every other S1 complete-run is byte-identical (LZ1 f5745/662, LZ2 f1068/1616, LZ3 f8499/1525, MZ2 f2823/1043, MZ3 f2079/1123, SBZ2 f1447/977, SLZ1 f2872/163, SLZ2 f2898/121, SLZ3 f814/1024, SYZ1 f4430/554, SYZ3 f6065/483, GHZ3 f6464/271, FZ f766/135) and GHZ1/GHZ2/SYZ2/SBZ3 GREEN. The earlier memory "fan-vs-wall / riser SolidObject negates the +2" hypothesis was DISPROVEN: there is no wall (ROM x_speed=0xE4, Sonic moving right freely, not blocked). Decisive ROM math: f2552 x=1806.1900 = f2551(1805.3500) + x_speed(0xE4), no +2 term; the fan FIRST pushes at f2553 (1808.F100 = f2552 + x_speed(0xD8) + 2px). So the engine pushes the fan ONE FRAME EARLY.

The 1px Y diff is execution order: Sonic RIDES the SLZ staircase (Obj5B) which re-seats his Y to 0210 each frame as he climbs steps. In ROM the staircase child Sonic rides is a HIGHER slot than the fan (Obj5D), so it re-seats AFTER the fan reads Y; the fan sees the pre-step-lift Y. The engine folds the staircase into a LOWER slot than the fan, so the live Y already reflects the step lift -> fan reads it -> pushes a frame early. The fan force itself is byte-perfect +2 (recomputed by hand: facingRight, no-reverse, pX=1806/pY=0210 -> +2, matching the engine and the f2556 in-air +2). docs/s1disasm/_incObj/5D SLZ Fan.asm:53-56,75.

Object-local (only the fan reads the snapshot; the capture is inert for all other objects). Earlier `getCentreY(1)` (previous-frame) experiment fixed f2552 but regressed f307 (-4px, a DIFFERENT airborne fan scenario), proving the faithful value is the exec-start Y, not the previous frame's.
- After: SLZ2 f2552 -> f2554 (f2552/f2553 now byte-match ROM). New frontier f2554 `y` exp=0x0211 act=0x0212 (+1) is the PARKED SLZ staircase ride-seat +1px-Y family (engine st=28 still pushing vs ROM st=20), unrelated to the fan. SLZ2 error count rises 137 -> 156 as the trace now reaches that deeper pre-existing root two frames later (frontier-advance downstream cascade, not a regression of previously-passing content).

- First error before fix: f5745 `camera_y` exp=0x028E act=0x028C (a 2px symptom). Diagnosed (engine-side, no BizHawk) with a temp per-frame dump of all Obj 63/6F instances + the trace's `object_near` ROM data: the LZ1 spawner `@1070,0280` (subtype 0x80, v_obj63 slot 0) fires once at f5281 and creates 8 child platforms (subtypes 0x00/0x02x3/0x04/0x05x3). The object's `isPersistent()` mirrors ROM `out_of_range` via `isInRangeAt(baseX)`, so an uninitialized platform reads as far off-screen and is unloaded by the exec loop's out-of-range pre-pass (`ObjectManager.updateCounterBasedExecThenLoad`, the line-714 `unloadCounterBasedOutOfRange` that runs BEFORE `executeObjectWithSolidContext`) on the spawn frame. ROM never hits this: `LabyrinthConvey` runs the routine (`LCon_Main`, which writes `objoff_30`) BEFORE the trailing `out_of_range.s loc_1236A,objoff_30(a0)` (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/63 LZ Conveyor.asm:5-13,53-63`; SBZ `SpinC_Main` identical, `docs/s1disasm/_incObj/6F SBZ Spin Platform Conveyor.asm:5-13,37-54`). The missing platforms removed the one ROM carries Sonic on at f5745: ROM walks him off slot 0x20 (f5736) and lands him on slot 0x48 @1012,02EE (f5745); the engine had no platform there so he free-fell.
- Fix: `isPersistent()` returns `true` while `!initialized` in both `Sonic1LZConveyorObjectInstance` and `Sonic1SpinConveyorObjectInstance` (the platform initializes on its update this frame; the next frame's check uses the real baseX). Object-local to Obj 63 / Obj 6F.
- After: LZ1 2214 -> 662 errors; first error stays at f5745 but is now `y` exp=0x02EE act=0x02ED (1px) — Sonic lands on the platform, 1px low. Cross-checked vs trace `object_near` ROM data: at f5671 two of the three left-side ascending platforms match ROM byte-for-byte (ROMs96 @1022,02D9 == eng @1022,02D9; ROMs97 @1022,0262 == eng @1022,0262), the lead one is 1px/1frame ahead (ROMs72 @1022,0351 vs eng @1022,0350) — a residual sub-pixel corner-rounding phase on a single platform, a distinct deeper root.
- LZ3 (f7952/1778) and SBZ1 (f3971/560) UNCHANGED — their frontiers diverge before/independent of this despawn race.
- Regression sweep (per-class surefire .txt): GHZ1 GREEN, GHZ2 GREEN, SYZ2 GREEN; every other S1 complete-run byte-identical (LZ2 f1068, LZ3 f7952, SBZ1 f3971, MZ1 f2089, MZ2 f2819/1116, MZ3 f2079/1123, SBZ2 f1395/1000, SLZ1 f164, SLZ2 f137, SLZ3 f1024, SYZ1 f360, SYZ3 f483, GHZ3 f6464). Units: `CollisionSystemTest`/`TestSolidRoutineProfiles`/`TestCollisionLogic`/`TestSonic1PlatformObjectInstanceRespawn` 69/0, `TestRewindCoverageGuard` (no new gap) + S3K `TestS3kAiz1SkipHeadless`/`TestSonic3kLevelLoading` 44/0.
## 2026-06-24 - Camera bottom-boundary airborne +8 acceleration deferred one frame to the camera clamp; S1 MZ1 f2089 -> f2101 (205 -> 204)

- Branch/worktree: `bugfix/ai-s1-camera` off `origin/develop` dae1bf67f (worktree `.worktrees/batbrain`).
- Command: `mvn test -Dmse=off "-Dtest=com.openggf.tests.trace.s1.TestS1Mz1CompleteRunTraceReplay" "-Dsurefire.argLine=-Xmx6g -Xshare:off"`.
- First error before fix: f2089 `camera_y` exp=0x02BE act=0x02C4 (6px). Player byte-identical to ROM (same sub-pixel, velocity); pure camera vertical-settle. Diagnosed by instrumenting `Camera.updateBoundaryEasing`: at f2089 (Sonic just airborne) the engine eased `maxY` 0x02BC -> 0x02C4 (+8, airborne acceleration) and then `updatePosition` clamped the boundary-pinned camera straight to 0x02C4 the SAME frame.
- Root: ROM `DeformLayers` runs `ScrollVertical` (camera move + clamp to the current `v_limitbtm2`) BEFORE `DynamicLevelEvents` (`docs/s1disasm/_inc/DeformLayers (REV01).asm:16-18`); `.move_boundary_down` accelerates the bottom boundary +2 -> +8/frame once Sonic is airborne and the camera is within 8px of it (`docs/s1disasm/_inc/DynamicLevelEvents.asm:35-49`). Since the boundary update runs AFTER the camera move, the +8 rate change is consumed by the NEXT frame's camera. The engine eases boundaries BEFORE moving the camera (`updateBoundaryEasing()` then `updatePosition()` in `LevelFrameStep`/`GameLoop`), so the +8 reached the camera one frame early. A global order swap (camera-move then ease) was tried and REJECTED — it regressed GHZ2 f3349 (the rising-boundary-under-roll case relies on the camera following the freshly-snapped boundary same-frame, ROM `SV_BottomBoundaryMoving`) and overshot MZ1 to f2019.
- Fix: a derived `cameraClampMaxY` that `updatePosition` clamps to instead of `maxY`. In the boundary-descending direction it advances by the step `maxY` took on the PREVIOUS frame (constant +2 keeps perfect pace; the +8 jump reaches the camera one frame late, matching ROM ScrollVertical reading the prior frame's `v_limitbtm2`). The ascending/snap path still uses `maxY` same-frame (GHZ2). `cameraClampMaxY` is derived: re-synced on `setMaxY` (immediate boundary writes) and reset to the converged value on rewind `restore`, so no `CameraSnapshot` field is needed.
- After: MZ1 f2089 -> f2101 (205 -> 204 errors). New frontier f2101 `camera_y` exp=0x02E8 act=0x02EA is a DEEPER root: with the camera-read timing fixed, the engine's underlying `maxY` boundary easing itself is ~6px ahead of ROM's `v_limitbtm2` during the +8->+2 deceleration tail (the camera becomes boundary-limited again and reads the diverged boundary). Precisely matching ROM's `v_limitbtm2` easing requires the recorder to capture `v_limitbtm2` per frame (not currently in the trace) — see follow-up. NOTE (from memory): MZ1 was previously characterized as non-greenable anyway (its 204-error count is dominated by a downstream ~f4230 physics cascade, not the camera).
- Regression sweep (with-fix vs no-fix baseline on dae1bf67f, first-error frame + count): GHZ1 GREEN, GHZ2 GREEN. All other S1 camera-affected complete-runs BYTE-IDENTICAL: LZ1 f5745/2214, GHZ3 f6464/271, SLZ1 f2872/164, SYZ1 f816/360. Cross-game shared-Camera check: S2 EHZ1 PASS, S3K AIZ f1095/4309 byte-identical. Camera units: `TestCamera`, `TestCameraRewindSnapshot`, `TestLookScrollDelay` PASS (36 tests, only the still-red MZ1 frontier fails as expected).
- Follow-up: extend the recorder to capture S1 `v_limitbtm2` (+`f_bgscrollvert`) per frame so the engine `maxY` easing can be matched to ROM exactly (closes MZ1 f2101 and any other boundary-convergence-tail camera blips). SYZ1 f816 `camera_x` (this task's other target) is NOT a pure camera bug: ROM `onObj=0x28` (Sonic rides the FloatingBlock @0200,03C3) but engine `ride=0` — a riding/position symptom (like LZ1/GHZ1's camera_y), to be chased object-side.

## 2026-06-23 - S1 Seesaw tilt target computed post-player (atomic ChkSide->ChgFrame); SLZ3 f745 -> f814

- Branch/worktree: `bugfix/ai-s1-slz3-f745` off `origin/develop` 55a2f5b16 (worktree `.worktrees/slz3-f718`).
- Command: `mvn test "-Dtest=com.openggf.tests.trace.s1.TestS1Slz3CompleteRunTraceReplay" -DfailIfNoTests=false "-Dsurefire.argLine=-Xmx6g -Xshare:off"`.
- First error before fix: f745 `y` exp=0x02D8 act=0x02DB (3px); also f756 (re-seat blip) and f786 (`y_speed` -0738, spikeball launch). Root diagnosed with the v3.5 `object_near` `obj_frame` aux (this session's recorder extension): the ROM seesaw (Obj 5E, slot 70) flips its tilt mapping frame `obj_frame` 0x02->0x01 at f745 (player rocking within 8px of centre x=0x740 -> See_ChkSide sets flat), while the engine flipped at f747 -- 2 frames late.
- Root: the engine latched the tilt target (`See_ChkSide`) in `onSolidContact`, which fires during the player's solid pass (BEFORE the post-physics object update), while `See_ChgFrame` (obFrame advance) ran in `update()`. Since `update()` runs after `onSolidContact` within the frame, See_ChgFrame advanced obFrame toward the PREVIOUS frame's target -> the tilt flip lagged a frame. ROM `See_Slope2` (routine 4, `docs/s1disasm/_incObj/5E SLZ Seesaw.asm:71-118`) runs `See_ChkSide` then falls straight into `See_ChgFrame`, both inside ExecuteObjects AFTER the player slot moved (atomic, post-move x). The trace had NO `x` divergence (engine and ROM player x identical every frame), so the only defect was WHEN the engine read the player x for the tilt decision.
- Fix: compute `calculateTargetAngle` (See_ChkSide) inside `update()` immediately before `updateMappingFrame` (See_ChgFrame), gated on the standing bit (still maintained by `onSolidContact`). S1 runs objects after player physics (`objectsExecuteAfterPlayerPhysics=true`), so `update()` observes Sonic's post-move x; this keeps the ROM ChkSide->ChgFrame order atomic and post-move. Object-local to Obj 5E.
- After: SLZ3 f745 -> f814. Resolved the f745/f756 tilt re-seat blips AND the f786 spikeball-launch cascade (all three gone from the error list). New frontier f814 `y_speed` exp=-0A80 act=0x0000 / `air` 1 vs 0 = a deeper spikeball launch divergence (ROM springs Sonic up ~10.5px, engine doesn't yet). Error count 916 -> 1024 (longer new cascade past a +69-frame-advanced frontier).
- Regression sweep: SLZ1 (f2872, 164 err) and SLZ2 (f1714, 215 err) BYTE-IDENTICAL; MZ3 (f2079, 1123 err) unchanged; GHZ1/GHZ2/SYZ2/SBZ3 stay GREEN. Object-local (seesaw only), so no shared-code cross-game sweep needed. Unit tests pass: `TestSeesawBallGraphRewind` 6/0, `TestS1SlzBossSpikeballGraphRewind` 5/0, `TestSonic1LargeGrassyPlatformObjectInstance` 3/0, `TestCollisionLogic` 1/0.

## 2026-06-23 - S1 Seesaw used a non-zero slope baseline so SlopeObject landing fired 1 frame late; SLZ3 f718 -> f745 (1073 -> 916)

- Branch/worktree: `bugfix/ai-s1-slz3-f718` off `origin/develop` 0b0fb8ac7 (worktree `.worktrees/slz3-f718`).
- Command: `mvn test "-Dtest=TestS1Slz3CompleteRunTraceReplay" -DfailIfNoTests=false "-Dsurefire.argLine=-Xmx6g -Xshare:off"`.
- First error before fix: f718 `y_speed` exp=0x0000 act=0x0610. ROM: rolling Sonic falling at y_speed=0x05D8 (f717) lands on the SLZ Seesaw (Obj 5E) at f718 — `y_speed` snaps to 0, `air` 1->0, `status` bit 3 set (on object), `g_speed = x_speed = -0168`. Engine kept falling (`y_speed=0x0610`, airborne) and only landed at f719 (one frame late).
- Root: `Sonic1SeesawObjectInstance.getSlopeBaseline()` returned `COLLISION_HEIGHT` (8). ROM `See_Slope` (routine 2, `docs/s1disasm/_incObj/5E SLZ Seesaw.asm:67`) lands the player via `SlopeObject`, which uses ABSOLUTE slope values: `d0 = obY(a0) - heightmapByte` with no baseline subtraction (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/sub PlatformObject.asm:150-152`, then `Plat_NoXCheck_AltY`). The engine's `resolveSlopedContact` computes `baseY = anchorY - (slopeSample - slopeBaseline)`, so a baseline of 8 placed the sampled top surface 8px LOWER (larger Y) than ROM's `obY - slopeSample`. The falling player therefore had to drop ~8px further before the engine registered the top-solid landing, delaying it by one frame at the trace's fall speed.
- Fix: `getSlopeBaseline()` returns 0, citing the ROM absolute-slope semantics and matching the sibling `SlopeObject` user `Sonic1CollapsingLedgeObjectInstance` (which already returns 0 for the same reason). Object-local to Obj 5E (SLZ-only). The riding re-seat path (`sampleSlopeY`) is already baseline-independent, so continued-ride Y is unchanged.
- After: SLZ3 f718 -> f745, 1073 -> 916 errors. New frontier f745 `y` exp=0x02D8 act=0x02DB (3px): a single-frame seesaw-tilt re-seat phase blip (f743/f744 match, f745 ROM re-seats the rider up 3px one frame before the engine, both agree again at f746; same blip recurs at f756). The next substantial divergence is f786 (`y_speed`/`air`, a deeper player-physics root). Both new roots are NOT this baseline bug.
- Regression sweep (vs develop baseline, A/B by temporarily reverting the single-line edit): SLZ1 f2872 (164 errors) and SLZ2 f1714 (215 errors) byte-identical with and without the fix; GHZ1, GHZ2, SYZ2 stay GREEN. Unit tests pass: `TestSonic1LargeGrassyPlatformObjectInstance` 3/0, `TestSeesawBallGraphRewind` 6/0, `TestS1SlzBossSpikeballGraphRewind` 5/0, `TestCollisionLogic` 1/0.
## 2026-06-23 - S1 LR spring control lock decremented in air; SLZ2 f1714 -> f2552 (215 -> 137)

- Branch/worktree: `bugfix/ai-s1-slz2-f1493` in worktree `.worktrees/slz2-f1493`, detached at `origin/develop` 0b0fb8ac7.
- Command: `mvn test "-Dtest=TestS1Slz2CompleteRunTraceReplay" -DfailIfNoTests=false "-Dsurefire.argLine=-Xmx6g -Xshare:off"`.
- **`s1_slz2` advanced f1714 -> f2552, errors 215 -> 137.** First error before fix: f1714 `x` exp=0x15F2 act=0x15F3 (engine 1px right; `x_speed`/`g_speed` exp=-0F94 act=-0F14, +0x80; `x_sub` ROM C500 vs engine 4500, +0x8000). After: f2552 `x` exp=0x1806 act=0x1808 — a distinct StaircaseObject (0x5B) ride-position root (`onObj`/`onSlot` 0x5B, `ride=1`).
- Root: the S1 LR spring (Obj 41) bounced Sonic leftward off a ledge at f06A2 with `locktime=15`. ROM `Spring_BounceLR` writes `move.w #15,locktime(a1)` (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/41 Springs.asm:145`); `locktime` (objoff_3E) is the same field S2's spring writes as `move_lock` (`docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:34031`). ROM only decrements `locktime` in `Sonic_SlopeRepel` (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/01 Sonic.asm:1383,1410`), called by the grounded modes `Sonic_MdNormal`/`Sonic_MdRoll` but NOT the airborne `Sonic_MdJump`/`MdJump2` — so during the 6 airborne frames (f06AA-f06AF) the lock is frozen. At f06B2 ROM still had the lock active and ignored the just-pressed Right input (inertia held at F06C); the engine modeled the lock with `springingFrames`, which `tickStatus()` decrements every frame including airborne, so the engine's lock had expired and it applied the Right-deceleration (F06C->F0EC). Verified frame-by-frame via a temp `OGGF_DBG_SLZ2` dump in the trace loop (engine matched ROM through f06B1, diverged at f06B2; with the fix `mlock` froze at 7 across the airborne frames and f06B2 held F06C / xsub C500 = ROM).
- Fix: `Sonic1SpringObjectInstance.applyHorizontalSpring` now also calls `player.setMoveLockTimer(15)` (engine model of `locktime`, decremented only on grounded frames in `doSlopeRepel()`). `springing` is retained for the air-spring animation / carry marker consumed elsewhere. Object-local to Obj 41's horizontal path; only `Spring_LR` sets `locktime` (vertical/down springs and S2/S3K springs are untouched).

All other S1 frontiers unchanged: FZ f713/155, GHZ3 f6464/271, LZ1 f5745/2214, LZ2 f1068/2150, LZ3 f7952/1778, MZ1 f2089/205, MZ2 f2819/1116, MZ3 f2079/1123, SBZ1 f2268/805, SBZ2 f1395/1000, SLZ3 f718/1073, SYZ3 f6065/483. SYZ1 frontier frame/field UNCHANGED (f816 `camera_x`) but downstream-cascade error count 351 -> 360 (+9) in an already-red trace (SYZ1 hits LR springs; the post-spring lock window shifts a few later cascade frames — no new earlier divergence). ## 2026-06-23 - S1 type-03 platform fall timer missed the landing frame; GHZ1 f3246 -> GREEN (255 -> 0)

- Branch/worktree: `bugfix/ai-s1-ghz1-advance` off `origin/develop` 88a4be974; cherry-picked Orbinaut CalcSine fix (f9fac6f25) first to restore SLZ2 to its correct develop baseline before the platform fix.
- **`s1_ghz1` GREENED (255 -> 0 errors).** First error before fix: f3246 `y` exp=0x0171 act=0x0170 / `camera_y` exp=0x0111 act=0x0110 (1px; Sonic 1px too high on a type-03 falling platform). After: complete-run passes with 0 errors.
- Root: ROM `Plat_Solid` (routine 2) calls `PlatformObject` — which sets `obStatus` bit 3 (standing) AND changes routine to 4 — then falls through to `Plat_Action` which calls `Plat_Move`. `.type03` (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/18 Platforms.asm:201-216`): `tst.w objoff_3A; bne .type03_wait; btst #3,obStatus; beq .nomove; move.w #30,objoff_3A`. So on the landing frame, the timer is set to 30. The engine's `moveFallOnStand()` runs BEFORE `checkpointAll()` (which is the engine's `PlatformObject` equivalent), so on the landing frame it read the PREVIOUS frame's `playerStanding=false`, missed the timer start, and started the 30-frame countdown 1 frame late. This meant the platform transitioned to type04 (falling, 16.16 gravity 0x38) 1 frame late, holding Sonic on the surface 1 frame longer. At GHZ1 f3246, the platform `@13A0,0188 subtype=03`: with correct timing the platform had already fallen 1px (type04 workingY advanced), setting its Y to 0x018D vs the engine's 0x018C; Sonic rode via `MvSonicOnPtfm2` (`platform.Y - 9 - 19`) = 0x0171 (ROM) vs engine 0x0170.
- Fix: after `checkpointAll()` sets `playerStanding` in `Sonic1PlatformObjectInstance.update`, added a post-checkpoint guard: `if (moveType == 0x03 && timer == 0 && playerStanding) { timer = FALL_STAND_DELAY; }`. This mirrors `.type03`'s first-time-standing detection on the landing frame. Object-local to Obj 18.
- Regression sweep (full S1 sweep, vs develop baseline including cherry-picked Orbinaut fix): GHZ2 GREEN, SYZ2 GREEN, all other S1 frontiers unchanged: GHZ3 f2693, LZ1 f5745, LZ2 f1068, LZ3 f6517, MZ1 f2089, MZ2 f2819, MZ3 f2079, SBZ1 f2268, SBZ2 f1395, SLZ1 f933, SLZ2 f1493, SLZ3 f718, SYZ1 f816, SYZ3 f6065. Unit tests: TestSolidRoutineProfiles 13/0, TestSonic1SpringObjectInstance 2/0, TestOrbinautBadnikInstance 6/0 — all pass.
- Note: this fix was developed in worktree `ghz1-advance` which was based on `origin/develop` 88a4be974 (before `f9fac6f25` Orbinaut fix). Without cherry-picking the Orbinaut fix first, the timer fix caused SLZ2 to regress from f1493 to f1016: the earlier platform fall timing changed Sonic's trajectory so he hit the Orbinaut spike 4 frames early (a pre-existing spike-orbit 1px Y offset that the Orbinaut fix addresses). Cherry-picking the Orbinaut fix into the branch first restored the correct behavior.

## 2026-06-23 - S1 SmashableWall setCentreX cleared sub-pixel on smash; GHZ3 f2693 -> f4650 (477 -> 363)

- Branch/worktree: `bugfix/ai-s1-ghz3-advance` off `origin/develop` (HEAD 8e3aefaaf).
- **`s1_ghz3` frontier advanced f2693 -> f4650 (477 -> 363 errors).** First error before fix: f2693 `x` exp=0x083C act=0x083B (1px too left). After: f4650 `x_speed` mismatch (next root, unrelated to this fix).
- Root: `Sonic1BreakableWallObjectInstance.smashWall` (lines 227/231 before fix) called `player.setCentreX((short) value)` to apply the ±4px x adjustment after smashing. ROM's equivalent (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/3C GHZ, SLZ Smashable Wall.asm` lines 57-64) uses `addq.w #4,obX(a1)` and `subq.w #8,obX(a1)` which modify ONLY the integer pixel word at `obX`, leaving `obSubX` (the sub-pixel word) intact. `setCentreX` clears the sub-pixel to 0. At f2691 (the smash frame), Sonic's sub-pixel was 0x1200 after the SolidObject snap (preserved correctly by the engine's `player.move` snap path). After the ROM-path `addq.w #4` the sub stays 0x1200, but the engine's `setCentreX` zeroed it to 0x0000. The accumulated sub-pixel difference meant that at f2693, Sonic's carry bit didn't fire (engine sub 0xF200+0x7600=no-carry, vs ROM sub 0x8E00+0x7600=carry), leaving the integer x 1px short.

## 2026-06-23 - S1 SpikedPoleHelix v_ani0_frame unseeded; GHZ3 f4650 -> f5043 (363 -> 6)

- Branch/worktree: `bugfix/ai-s1-ghz3-f4650` off `origin/develop` (HEAD c1a59c238).
- **`s1_ghz3` frontier advanced f4650 -> f5043 (363 -> 6 errors).** First error before fix: f4650 `x_speed` exp=0x0194 act=-0x0200 (sign flip; engine in HURT state, ROM grounded and running right). After: f5043 `x_speed` mismatch (next root).
- Root: `Sonic1SpikedPoleHelixObjectInstance` maintained per-object `animCounter=0` / `animTimer=11` fields initialized at construction (object spawn), ignoring the ROM's global `v_ani0_frame` counter which has been ticking since level start. At GHZ3 f4650 (gfc=0x1220), ROM `v_ani0_frame` = `(-ceil(0x1220/12)) & 7 = (-387) & 7 = 5`, so that particular spike was harmless (frame ≠ 0). The engine's `animCounter` had diverged from this phase, placing the spike at frame 0 (harmful), triggering a HURT on Sonic.
- Root type: identical to SBZ Electrocuter (commit `SBZ1 f1925`) — object reads a ROM global counter via per-object unseeded state instead of the trace-seeded level frame counter.
- Root (ROM): `Hel_RotateSpikes` (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/17 GHZ Spiked Pole Helix.asm:95-105`): `move.b (v_ani0_frame).w,d0` — reads the GLOBAL `v_ani0_frame` (RAM 0xFEC1). `SynchroAnimate` (`docs/s1disasm/sonic.asm:3111-3119`) ticks `v_ani0_frame` every 12 `v_framecount` (gfc) ticks, starting with an underflow tick at gfc=1 (initial `v_ani0_time=0`). After gfc=N: `v_ani0_frame = (-ceil(N/12)) & 7` where `ceil(N/12) = (N+11)/12` (integer division).
- Fix: replaced the per-object `animCounter` accumulation in `update()` with a direct derivation from the trace-seeded level frame counter: `gfc = levelManager.getFrameCounter()+1; animCounter = (-((gfc + 11) / 12)) & 7`. This is computed every frame, matching ROM's read of the shared `v_ani0_frame`. Object-local to Obj 0x17 (GHZ-only).
- Regression sweep (full S1 broad sweep, vs develop baseline c1a59c238): GHZ1 GREEN, GHZ2 GREEN, SYZ2 GREEN. All other S1 frontiers byte-identical: LZ1 f5745, LZ2 f1068, LZ3 f6517, MZ1 f2089, MZ2 f2819, MZ3 f2079, SBZ1 f2268, SBZ2 f1395, SLZ1 f933, SLZ2 f1493, SLZ3 f718, SYZ1 f816, SYZ3 f6065. No unit test for helix (none existed).
## 2026-06-23 - S1 Staircase timer no-decrement on set frame + SolidObject airHalfHeight for fresh contacts; SLZ1 f933 -> f2872 (246 -> 164)

- Branch/worktree context: `bugfix/ai-s1-slz1-staircase` off `develop` 85edc9384.
- **`s1_slz1` advanced f933 -> f2872, errors 246 -> 164.** First error before: f933 `y` 1px (Sonic seated 1px too low on Obj 0x5B Staircase). After: f2872 `y` 1px (cascade — ROM Sonic on a CirclingPlatform, engine Sonic still on the staircase; caused by pre-staircase ring-count and x-position cascades).
- Root 1 (f933 timer): `Sonic1StaircaseObjectInstance.updateType00` ran the timer decrement on the same frame the timer was set. ROM `Stair_Type00` (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/5B SLZ Staircase.asm:104-119`): `tst.w timer; bne.s loc_10FC0; cmpi.b #1,playerTop; bne.s locret_10FBE; move.w #$1E,timer` then falls through to `locret_10FBE rts` — the decrement at `loc_10FC0` is only entered when the timer was already non-zero. Engine collapsed set+decrement into one frame, advancing the countdown by 1 each trigger. Fixed by `return` after `timer = TOP_CONTACT_DELAY` in both `updateType00` and `updateType02`. Same pattern in `Stair_Type02` at asm:122-137 (`move.w #$3C, timer` + fall-through to `locret_10FDE`).
- Root 2 (f2526–f2529 sibling snap): `processMultiPieceCollision` runs all non-riding pieces of the staircase with `resolveContact(apply=true)`. Non-riding sibling pieces at overlapping X ranges were applying `Solid_Landed` Y snaps that overrode the ridden-piece re-seat. In ROM, each piece occupies a separate SST slot; the ridden piece (higher slot) runs LAST and its `MvSonicOnPtfm`/`SolidObject` result is authoritative. Fix: track `ridingCentreYToRestore` from `processInlineRidingObject`, gate `putRidingState` on `ridingCentreYToRestore == MIN_VALUE`, and restore after the sibling pass.
- Root 3 (f2526–f2872 1px grounded snap): `processMultiPieceCollision` used `groundHalfHeight=17` for grounded players. ROM `SolidObject_cont` (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/sub SolidObject.asm:170-176`; S2 equivalent `s2.asm:35361-35373`) always uses d2 (airHalfHeight=16) for the Y bounding-box window: `add.w y_radius, d2` where d2 is the input top half-height. Using `groundHalfHeight` inflated `maxTop` by 1, giving `distY=4` (engine) vs `distY=3` (ROM) and snapping Sonic 1px too low (`newCentreY = playerCentreY - 4 + 3 = -1` vs `-3 + 3 = 0`). Fix: unconditionally use `params.airHalfHeight()` in `processMultiPieceCollision` (correct for S1/S2/S3K — all three ROM `SolidObject` implementations use the top half-height in d2 for Y detection; `groundHalfHeight` is only used by `MvSonicOnPtfm` for the continued-ride re-seat).
- Regression sweep (vs develop baseline, first-error frame + count): GHZ2 GREEN, SYZ2 GREEN. All other S1 frontiers byte-identical: FZ f713/155, GHZ1 f3246/255, GHZ3 f2693/477, LZ1 f5745/2185, LZ2 f1068/2150, LZ3 f6517/1726, MZ1 f2089/205, MZ2 f2819/1116, MZ3 f2079/1123, SBZ1 f2268/805, SBZ2 f1395/1000, SLZ2 f1714/215, SLZ3 f718/1073, SYZ1 f816/351, SYZ3 f6065/483. 66 pre-existing unit test failures unaffected (rewind torture, MhzMushroomCap, TestNoServicesInObjectConstructors, TestTouchResponseManager, TestPlayableSpriteMovement — all present on develop baseline). Staircase unit tests: TestSonic1StaircaseActivation and TestSonic1StaircaseWallCollision pass.

## 2026-06-23 - S1 SpikedPoleHelix animCounter off-by-one + hurt-direction source X; GHZ3 f5043 -> f6464 (6 -> 271)

- Branch/worktree: `bugfix/ai-s1-ghz3-f5043` off `origin/develop`.
- **`s1_ghz3` frontier advanced f5043 -> f6464 (6 -> 271 errors).** First error before fix: f5043 `y_speed` exp=0 act=-0x0400 (HURT from @1688 helix spike at 0x16C8). After: f6464 `y` mismatch (different root).
- Root 1 — animCounter off-by-one: ROM `Level_MainLoop` runs `ExecuteObjects` at sonic.asm:2988 BEFORE `SynchroAnimate` at 3010. Objects at loop iteration gfc=N therefore read `v_ani0_frame` set by the PREVIOUS iteration's SynchroAnimate (after N-1 calls). The prior formula computed `ceil(N/12) = (N+11)/12` ticks (value after N calls), which is 1 tick too many when N is a multiple of 12. Correct formula: `(-((gfc+10)/12)) & 7` = value after (N-1) calls. At trace f5042 (gfc=5029), the old formula gave animCounter=4 making the phase=4 spike (@16C8) harmful; the correct value is 5 (phase=4 → (5+4)&7=1, harmless). The spurious hurt fired 1 trace-frame early.
- Root 2 — hurt-direction source X: ROM `HurtSonic.checkDirection` (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/Sonic ReactToItem.asm:402-405) compares Sonic's `obX` against `obX(a2)` where `a2` = the individual child spike's RAM slot (x=0x16C8). Engine `applyHurt` used `instance.getX()` (parent helix x=0x1688). Sonic (x=0x16C6) > parent (0x1688), so engine negated → rightward bounce (+0x200). Correct: Sonic (0x16C6) < spike (0x16C8), so no negate → leftward (-0x200). Fix: added `regionX` field to `TouchResponseResult`; `processMultiRegionTouch` populates it from `region.x()`; `applyHurt` prefers `result.regionX()` when present.
- Regression sweep: GHZ1 GREEN, GHZ2 GREEN, SYZ2 GREEN. 36 unit tests pass.

## 2026-06-23 - S1 Orbinaut satellite orbit used float Math.round instead of ROM CalcSine integer shift; SLZ2 f1016 -> f1493

- Branch: `bugfix/ai-s1-syz-slz-advance` off `develop` 326de21ad.
- **`s1_slz2` advanced f1016 -> f1493, errors 221 -> 277 (different cascade, higher total but later first-error).** First error before: f1016 `g_speed` exp=0x0295 act=0x0000 (hurt bounce; engine took early HURT from Orbinaut spike). After: f1493 `x` 1px on slope (a separate downstream frontier).
- Root: `OrbSpikeObjectInstance.update` computed orbital position with `Math.round(Math.cos(radians) * 16.0)`. ROM `Orb_CircleSpikeball` (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/60 Badnik - Orbinaut.asm:181-191`) calls `jsr CalcSine` (d0=sine, d1=cosine; range -0x100..0x100) then `asr.w #4,d1` / `add.w obX(a1),d1` for X, same for sine/Y. The arithmetic right shift truncates: sine=0xFE=254, `254 >> 4 = 15`; floating-point: `Math.round(254.0/256.0 * 16.0) = Math.round(15.875) = 16`. At SLZ2 f1016, spike Y was ROM 0x00B7 vs engine 0x00B8 (1px low). Player touch-box top at 0x00BC; spike bottom ROM 0x00B7+4=0x00BB (misses), engine 0x00B8+4=0x00BC (boundary hit → HURT fires 4 frames early). In ROM, Sonic wasn't hurt until f1020 after moving into the spike.
- Fix: replace float trig with `TrigLookupTable.sinHex(angle) >> 4` and `TrigLookupTable.cosHex(angle) >> 4` in `OrbSpikeObjectInstance.update` (`Sonic1OrbinautBadnikInstance.java`). Added `TrigLookupTable` import.
- Regression sweep (vs develop baseline, first-error frame + count): SYZ2 stays GREEN; GHZ2 stays GREEN. All LZ/SBZ frontiers unchanged: LZ1 f5745/2185, LZ2 f1068/2150, LZ3 f6517/1726, SBZ1 f2268/805, SBZ2 f1395/1000. ## 2026-06-22 - S1 LR spring used an exclusive right edge so a flush side contact never fired; SYZ1 f502 -> f816 (484 -> 351)

- Branch/worktree context: `bugfix/ai-syz1-advance` off `develop` cebf130d6.
- **`s1_syz1` advanced f502 -> f816, errors 484 -> 351.** First error before: f502 `camera_y` (a SYMPTOM; the driving divergence is `g_speed`/`x_speed` exp=0x1000 act=0x0000 — ROM spring-launched right, engine stopped). After: f816 `camera_x` (1px, a separate downstream frontier).
- Root (BizHawk + ROM physics.csv + engine debug; SYZ1 offset 61548, replay f502 = gfc 0x1F7): ROM launches Sonic RIGHT at 0x1000 via a horizontal (LR) spring (Obj41 subtype 0x10, @0218,03C2) — Sonic falls flush against the spring's right side and `Spring_LR` (after `SolidObject` sets Sonic's push bit) bounces him (x 022B->0223 via `subi #16,obX`/`neg obVelX`, xspd->0x1000). Deciding-question check (engine `getCentreY()` vs the trace physics.csv reference, anchored by `gameplay_frame_counter`): the fall positions MATCH ROM **frame-for-frame** and BOTH land at f502 at the same y=03BD — it is NOT a fall-timing or land-band off-by-one. The only difference is the land OUTCOME. The miss: the engine's SolidObject contact x-range gate (`ObjectSolidContactController`: `relX >= 2*halfWidth -> reject`) EXCLUDES the right edge, but ROM `SolidObject` `Solid_ChkCollision` (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/sub SolidObject.asm:160-166`, `cmp d3,d0; bhi Solid_NoCollision`) rejects only when STRICTLY greater than `2*halfWidth` — the right edge (Sonic flush against the object's right face) still collides. The LR spring's right solid edge (`0218 + 19 = 022B`) equals Sonic's centre x (`022B`), so `relX == 2*halfWidth` and the contact was rejected; the spring side contact never fired, so `Spring_LR` never set the push bit and Sonic fell to terrain (xspd 0).
- Fix: the spring's `getSolidRoutineProfile()` now returns `fullSolid(usesStickyContactBuffer(), /*inclusiveRightEdge*/ true, false)`. The engine already has the `inclusiveRightEdge` `SolidRoutineProfile` flag (used `true` by `Sonic1GirderBlock`/`Junction`/`PushBlock`/`InvisibleBarrier`); the spring was using the single-arg `fullSolid` which defaults it `false`. Object-local to Obj41. Updated `TestSonic1SpringObjectInstance.exposesFullSolidRoutineProfileForVerticalAndHorizontalSprings` (it asserted `inclusiveRightEdge=false`; now `true`, ROM-cited).
- Regression sweep (vs develop baseline, first-error frame + count): all other S1 complete-runs byte-identical (GHZ1 f3246/255, GHZ3 f2693/477, MZ1 f2089/205, MZ2 f2578/1010, MZ3 f2079/1048, LZ1 f5745/2185, LZ2 f1068/2150, LZ3 f6517/1726, SLZ1 f933/246, SLZ2 f1016/221, SLZ3 f718/1073, SBZ1 f2268/805, SBZ2 f1395/1000, SYZ2 green, SYZ3 f3476/485, FZ f713/155). GHZ2 + SBZ3 GREEN. S2 EHZ1 green; S3K AIZ f1095/4309 identical. ## 2026-06-22 - S1 off-screen self-delete badnik respawn; MZ2 f2578 -> f2819

Sonic, rolling and falling (`y_vel` +0x530+gravity = +0x568), rolls into the head; ROM `React_BadnikHit` (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/Sonic ReactToItem.asm:298-305`) negates his falling `y_vel` to **-0x568** to bounce him up. The engine had **no Caterkiller at all** there (the temp trace diagnostic + CATSCAN showed the engine Caterkiller despawned ~f1065 after walking off-screen and never respawned), so Sonic fell through to terrain at f2581 — all 1010 errors cascaded from this.

## 2026-06-22 - DEZ jet-stomp reads targeting sensor 1 frame late; DEZ1 f5261->f5952, errors 98->46

- Branch/worktree context: `bugfix/ai-dez1-green` (builds on the group-anim $C0 + boss-id boundary fixes below).
- **`s2_dez1` advanced f5261 -> f5952, errors 98 -> 46, roots 5 -> 3.** First error before: f5261 `y_speed` sign-flip (jet-stomp bounce miss). After: f5952 `y_speed` exp=0x0098 act=-0098 (a later jet-stomp; small residual drift remains).
- Root: BizHawk phase-alignment of the jet-stomp cycle (engine fc = trace-1) showed, after the $C0 fix, the body's pa06(spawn)->pa0A(recovery) span was 227 frames vs ROM 228 — the engine lost 1 frame in the descent/sensor region per jet-stomp, re-drifting the attack clock (ascent-start Δ +1/0/-1/-2 across jet-stomps). The body's wait-for-sensor phase updated `ChildObjC7_TargettingSensor` inline and read `targetedPlayerX` the SAME frame, so the descent began the frame the sensor reported. ROM `loc_3D784` reads the body's `objoff_28` at the body's frame start, but the sensor is a higher-slot object that runs AFTER the body in ExecuteObjects and writes `objoff_28` on its lock-on-report frame (`loc_3DE62`), so the body observes the report ONE frame later.
- Fix: capture `targetedPlayerX` BEFORE advancing the sensor child, then advance the sensor (for next frame). Restores the one-frame report latency; the descent starts on ROM's frame. Errors 98 -> 46.
- Regression: object-local (`Sonic2DeathEggRobotInstance`, DEZ-only). Residual: a smaller attack-clock drift (~1 frame / 2 jet-stomps) still misses the f5952 bounce; under investigation.

## 2026-06-22 - DEZ Death Egg Robot group-anim end-marker frame collapses DEZ1 127->98, advances f4007->f4933

- Branch/worktree context: `bugfix/ai-dez1-green` (worktree off `develop`).
- Command: `mvn -q -Dmse=relaxed test "-Dtest=TestS2DezEndingLevelSelectTraceReplay" -DfailIfNoTests=false "-Dsurefire.argLine=-Xmx6g -Xshare:off"`.
- **`s2_dez1` / `TestS2DezEndingLevelSelectTraceReplay` advanced f4007 -> f4933, errors 127 -> 98.** First error before: f4007 `y_speed`/`x_speed` velocity sign-flips (Death Egg Robot bounce miss). First error after: f4933 `x_speed` exp=0x0000 act=0x02DC (a later attack; residual 1-frame sensor-report drift).
- Root: the boss group-animation player `Sonic2DeathEggRobotInstance.stepGroupAnimation` returned "script complete" on the same frame the last keyframe's substeps finished, but ROM `ObjC7_GroupAni` (`loc_3E1AA`) terminates each script with a `$C0` end-marker keyframe processed on a SEPARATE frame (reads `anim_frame` at frame start: last real substep frame N advances `anim_frame` to `$C0`; frame N+1 reads `$C0` -> `loc_3E23E`/`loc_3E27E`/`loc_3E236` returns done with no deltas). So every ROM script costs one extra completion frame (off_3E3D0 crouch `0,1,2,$C0` = 41f not 40f; off_3E30A walk `0..8,$C0`). The engine omitted the marker, so every group-anim-gated attack-phase transition (crouch, walk-punch, stand-up walk) advanced one frame early. BizHawk-measured: the engine attack clock drifted progressively behind ROM (jet-stomp ascent-start Δ -2/-5/-7 across attacks), so by the f4007 jet-stomp the targeting-sensor lock-on snapped 7-8 frames early (engine trace f3877 vs ROM f3885, player moving left ~240/frame), the descent stomped at x=0x815 vs ROM 0x80E, and the body sat ~+5x/+8y of ROM at the bounce frame, missing the player's roll-up bounce box (`Touch_Enemy` neg.w x_vel/y_vel, s2.asm:85318-85345).
- Fix: model the `$C0` end-marker frame — when the substep advance lands `groupAnimFrameIdx == sequence.length`, fall through WITHOUT returning true (no deltas; last real keyframe's deltas already applied this frame); the next call's top-of-method end check returns done. Re-measured: jet-stomp ascent-start Δ collapses to 0/+1 through f4007, the f4007 bounce connects. Object-local to `Sonic2DeathEggRobotInstance` (the Death Egg Robot spawns only in DEZ), so no other zone/trace is affected.
- Regression: object-local change; no shared code touched. CNZ1 first-error held at its develop baseline f1691 (downstream count only); EHZ1/ARZ1/MCZ1/SCZ/WFZ stay green; S1 GHZ2 untouched (S1, different game). No frontier regressed.
- Residual (NOT in this commit): f4933 onward, a later jet-stomp still has a ~1-frame sensor lock-on report drift (the body ph06->ph08 descent-start reads the sensor's reported X one frame off ROM's pa06->pa08 handoff). Separate sensor/body update-order alignment; tracked for a follow-up. See memory `dez1-f4007-boss-body-position`.

## 2026-06-22 - S1 headroom ceiling-probe double-flip advances SYZ2 f1088 -> f6845

- Branch/worktree context: `bugfix/ai-syz2-advance` (worktree off current `develop`; develop confirmed ancestor).
- Command: `mvn -q -Dmse=relaxed test "-Dtest=TestS1Syz2CompleteRunTraceReplay" -DfailIfNoTests=false -Ds1.rom.path=s1.gen "-Dsurefire.argLine=-Xmx6g -Xshare:off"`.
- SYZ2 before: f1088 `x_speed` exp=0x02E8 actual=0x02F4 (311 errors). After: f6845 `x` exp=0x211A actual=0x211C (55 errors). Frontier advanced ~5757 frames; error count 311 -> 55.
- Root cause: at f1088 the BK2 input adds the jump button (0x08 -> 0x18) and ROM jumps (y_speed -0680, air/rolling) while the engine keeps ground-accelerating (x_speed 0x02E8 -> 0x02F4). The engine detected the jump press but `doJump()` was blocked: `getTerrainHeadroomDistance` returned 3 (< the 6px `Sonic_Jump` gate, `docs/s1disasm/_incObj/01 Sonic.asm:1180-1190`). The left ceiling probe hits SYZ2 collision tile 0x0093 (a left overhang; `rom[0x62A00+0x93*16]` = F7 F8 F9 FA FC FD FE 00..., verified identical to the engine's loaded tile by reading the ROM file directly — NOT a load bug). The headroom CalcRoomOverHead quadrant-0x80 probe pre-applied the `eori.w #$F` ceiling flip as a `dy` offset (`xorDelta`), but the engine's `Direction.UP` `scanVertical`/`calculateVerticalDistance` already models that flip — so it was DOUBLE-applied, yielding distance 3 instead of 8.
- BizHawk capture (this is the decisive evidence; bk2 offset 71507, f72595 = trace f1088; `Sonic_FindCeiling` hooks at 0x156CE/0x156D2): ROM obX=0x074F, obWidth=9, left probe d3=0x0746 column 6 — ALL identical to the engine — but ROM `leftDist(d1)=8 rightDist(d0)=7` (min 7 >= 6 -> JUMPS). ROM `FindFloor` (`sub FindNearestTile & FindFloor & FindWall.asm:163-167`) negates the -2 ceiling height to +2 and returns `15 - (2 + (probeY&$F=5)) = 8`. The engine's UP path returns exactly 8 WITHOUT the pre-flip.
- Fix: `CollisionSystem.describeCalcRoomOverHeadProbes` quadrant 0x80 drops the `xorDelta` Y pre-offset (`dy=0`), letting `scanVertical` own the single ceiling flip — matching the ordinary ceiling-sensor path. One file, `src/main/java/com/openggf/physics/CollisionSystem.java`. Shared S1/S2/S3K ceiling-probe code; game-agnostic.
- Regression sweep (fix vs clean detached-`develop` baseline, first-error frame + error count): SYZ2 f1088/311 -> f6845/55 (advance). GHZ3 f2693/492 -> f2693/477 (same frame, FEWER errors). GHZ1 f2790/436, LZ1 f5745/2185, SLZ1 f723/661, SLZ3 f718/1073, SLZ2 f1016/221 — byte-identical. GHZ2 stays GREEN (0 errors). MZ1 first-error frame UNCHANGED at f2089; total count 185 -> 205, entirely within its pre-existing f4230+ physics cascade (a region already fully divergent and non-greenable; no new earlier divergence). S2 EHZ1 green, ARZ green, CPZ f3365/310 identical. S3K AIZ f1095/4309, ICZ f3139/3179, LBZ f2270/5881 identical; TestS3kAiz1SkipHeadless passes. No frontier regressed.

## 2026-06-22 - S1 camera bottom-boundary follow GREENS GHZ2 (TestS1Ghz2CompleteRunTraceReplay 0 errors)

- Branch/worktree context: `bugfix/ai-s1-camera-vsettle` (worktree off current `develop`; develop confirmed ancestor). Base already carries the Obj18 platform-jump fix (develop b69c2c6ca) that took GHZ2 to f3349.
- Command: `mvn -Dmse=off test "-Dtest=TestS1Ghz2CompleteRunTraceReplay" -DfailIfNoTests=false -Ds1.rom.path=s1.gen "-Dsurefire.argLine=-Xmx6g -Xshare:off"`.
- GHZ2 before: f3349 `camera_y` expected=0x034A actual=0x034C (2 errors). After: **GREEN, 0 errors.** GHZ2 is the first S1 complete-run trace to go fully green.
- Root cause: the engine's vertical camera lagged a rising bottom level boundary by one frame. When the player rolls fast into a new lower area, `DynamicLevelEvents` (`docs/s1disasm/_inc/DynamicLevelEvents.asm:5-49`) eases `v_limitbtm2` toward `v_limitbtm1` at 2px/frame and sets `f_bgscrollvert=1` BEFORE `ScrollVertical`. ROM `ScrollVertical` then branches `SV_OnGround` -> (f_bgscrollvert set) `SV_BottomBoundaryMoving` (`docs/s1disasm/_inc/ScrollHoriz & ScrollVertical.asm:157-158,210`) -> `SV_SweetSpot` -> `SV_BottomBoundary` (line 259), clamping the camera to the freshly-moved boundary EVEN on a sweet-spot frame where the normal scroll produced no movement. The engine's `Camera.updatePosition` bottom-boundary clamp was gated only on `y != yBeforeVerticalScroll`, so on a sweet-spot frame (vertical scroll produced no movement) it skipped the clamp and the camera held its old y while `maxY` (engine mirror of `v_limitbtm2`) had already eased past it. BizHawk capture (bk2 offset 6622, ScrollVertical hook at 0x69AA + boundary poll): boundary eases 0x0400 -> 0x0300 under a grounded fast roll-land (g_speed ~0x0DE1, rolling); ROM camY reaches 0x034A at the divergence frame while the engine held 0x034C because its sweet-spot frame skipped the boundary clamp.
- Fix: `Camera.updatePosition` bottom-boundary clamp condition widened from `if (!lastFrameWrapped && y != yBeforeVerticalScroll)` to `if (!lastFrameWrapped && (y != yBeforeVerticalScroll || maxYChanging))`. `maxYChanging` is the engine's existing `f_bgscrollvert` mirror, set by `updateBoundaryEasing` (called before `updatePosition`). Shared S1/S2/S3K `ScrollVertical` behaviour; game-agnostic (no zone/game branch).
- Regression sweep (this branch vs clean detached-`develop` baseline, first-error frame + error count): S1 GHZ1 f2790/436, GHZ3 f2693/537, MZ1 f2089/185, LZ1 f5745/2185, SLZ1 f723/661, SLZ3 f718/1073 — ALL byte-identical. S2 EHZ1 green, ARZ level-select green, CPZ level-select f3365 `tails_x`/310 — identical.
